strengths: Strong and consistent experimental results on extrapolation tasks with substantial improvements (e.g., +7.3 PSNR on Shark over Grid4D baseline) while maintaining comparable reconstruction quality
Well-motivated problem: identifies genuine gap between reconstruction methods (no dynamics learning) and physics-informed methods (manual priors required); proposes reasonable middle ground

Comprehensive experimental evaluation across three diverse benchmarks (NVFi synthetic, PanopticSports real-world) with multiple baselines and detailed ablation study showing contribution of each component
Technically sound approach with well-reasoned design: separation of local and global feature encoding respects motion structure; Neural ODEs appropriate for continuous dynamics modeling
Clear presentation with helpful diagrams and distinction from prior work; adequate implementation details provided in appendix for reproducibility
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: primarily combines existing components (InstantNGP hash encoding, PointNet-based features, Neural ODEs); contribution is architectural rather than conceptual

Critical generalization limitation explicitly acknowledged by authors: no cross-dataset evaluation; method 'relies on specific training data'; proposed pretraining solution is speculative and untested—severely restricts practical applicability

Overstated 'prior-free' claim: affine transformation decoder (Eq. 7) encodes motion priors (rotation, scaling, shearing); architectural choices represent implicit domain assumptions; conflates 'no manual physics equations' with 'no priors'

Insufficient technical clarity on key components: Eq. 6 ambiguous about whether local features l are fixed or evolved; affine decomposition strategy (A.1) into many components lacks justification; global feature encoding complexity (FPS+KNN+PointNet+Transformer+pooling) not ablated

Incomplete reconstruction-extrapolation tradeoff analysis: PanopticSports shows notable reconstruction drops (e.g., Boxes: -1.7 PSNR vs Grid4D); claim of 'comparable reconstruction' undermined in some cases; no systematic analysis of quality sacrificed for extrapolation

Missing critical analyses: no computational cost/timing comparisons; only RK4 solver tested with no ablation; limited temporal extrapolation horizon tested; no failure mode discussion; no interpretation of learned dynamics

Dataset scope limitations: NVFi relatively simple/synthetic; PanopticSports has sparse viewpoints; no truly complex real-world sequences; relatively predictable motions (rigid, elastic, sports) tested

Incomplete experimental details: learning rate schedules unspecified; training steps vary (50k-80k) without justification; single-run results without error bars; hyperparameter sensitivity analysis absent

strengths: Addresses an important and underexplored problem of motion extrapolation for dynamic 3D scenes
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple datasets with comparisons to multiple state-of-the-art baselines
Strong quantitative improvements on synthetic NVFi benchmarks, with substantial gains in extrapolation metrics (e.g., ~8 PSNR improvement over GSPrediction)
Intuitive formulation: treating Gaussians as particles with evolving latent dynamics states is conceptually reasonable
Ablation study (Table 4) demonstrates contribution of key components
Qualitative results show visually plausible extrapolations compared to baselines
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: primarily combines existing techniques (InstantNGP hash encoding, PointNet-style feature encoding, Neural ODEs) without substantial innovation in any component

Core claims about learning dynamics are unsubstantiated: zero analysis or visualization of what the learned ODE function actually captures; no evidence of discovering physically meaningful patterns beyond sequence fitting

Severe generalization limitation inadequately addressed: model requires per-scene training with no cross-sequence generalization demonstrated, severely limiting practical applicability and contradicting claims about learning generalizable dynamics
Weak real-world performance: improvements on PanopticSports (Table 3) are marginal (<1 PSNR) and inconsistent, with reconstruction quality trade-offs not rigorously analyzed
Experimental design concerns: NVFi's fixed 0.75 split limits extrapolation distance to ~0.25 time units; no comparison with simple velocity-based baselines; no extrapolation degradation curves

Reconstruction-extrapolation trade-off poorly analyzed despite being acknowledged; Table 3 shows cases where lower reconstruction PSNR doesn't improve extrapolation, undermining the core design rationale

Technical design choices lack justification: why do spatial features (hash encoding) capture temporal dynamics? Why keep local features static while evolving global features? Affine decomposition motivation unclear

Incomplete ablation study: removes entire modules but lacks granular ablations on architectural choices (feature dimensions, ODE width, encoding resolution); Table 4 shows affine transformations have minimal impact

Misleading framing: 'prior-free' claim overstated (strong architectural priors remain); 'first end-to-end dynamics learning' ignores prior Neural ODE 4D work; 'general method' contradicted by scene-specific training requirement

Reproducibility and rigor issues: no error bars or confidence intervals; no statistical significance testing; arbitrary hyperparameter choices lack justification; computational costs not reported; code not available for review

strengths: Well-motivated problem formulation addressing the important gap between dynamic 3D reconstruction and extrapolation without manually defined physical priors
Comprehensive experimental validation on multiple benchmarks (NVFi synthetic, PanopticSports real) with systematic comparison against reconstruction and extrapolation baselines
Strong and consistent improvements on extrapolation task (e.g., +7.9 PSNR on Shark, +9.8 PSNR on Chessboard vs. nearest competitor) while maintaining competitive reconstruction quality
Principled technical architecture with clear separation of local and global feature encoding, demonstrating understanding of motion vs. appearance modeling
Effective ablation study (Table 4) convincingly demonstrates necessity of latent dynamics state, Neural ODE module, and affine deformations
Clear presentation with well-designed figures (especially Figure 1) effectively communicating the key insight and differentiating from prior work
weaknesses: Critical generalization limitation acknowledged in appendix: method requires per-scene/dataset retraining and lacks cross-scene generalization, severely restricting practical applicability despite 'general' claims

Insufficient analysis of learned dynamics: no visualization of learned differential equations, no verification that the model discovers physically meaningful patterns rather than merely fitting trajectories
Modest improvements on realistic data: on PanopticSports human motion capture (~0.3 PSNR gain), suggesting limited advantage for complex real-world scenarios requiring ground truth physics
Reconstruction-extrapolation trade-off underexplored: several cases show lower reconstruction PSNR (Boxes: -1.7 PSNR vs. Grid4D), with limited analysis of when/why this occurs
Narrow temporal extrapolation windows: evaluation limited to 0.1-0.25 of training sequence; stability for longer horizons (2-3x) remains unknown
Incremental technical novelty: individual components (hash encoding, PointNet aggregation, Neural ODEs) are established; primary contribution is their combination for this specific problem
Incomplete comparative analysis with GaussianPrediction: over-simplified explanation of why GNNs fail at temporal dynamics; GaussianPrediction remains competitive on real data
Missing computational analysis: no runtime measurements, inference cost of Neural ODE integration not reported, practical scalability unclear
Limited dataset complexity: experiments use relatively simple synthetic objects and sports sequences; more complex scenes with fluid dynamics or cloth would strengthen claims
Statistical rigor issues: no error bars, confidence intervals, or multi-run validation reported; unclear if results are stable across random seeds

strengths: Well-motivated problem: clearly identifies why time-conditioned methods fail at extrapolation and proposes principled Neural ODE-based solution
Efficient architecture: factorization of state into static and dynamic components reduces complexity O(NG) → O(FG), inspired by Material Point Method
Comprehensive experiments: four datasets, multiple baseline categories, extensive ablations validating each component; achieves ~5 dB over time-conditioned and ~2.5 dB over velocity field methods
Strong empirical results: consistent state-of-the-art extrapolation performance while maintaining competitive reconstruction quality
Clear presentation: well-written with effective visualizations, pedagogical toy experiment, and thorough supplementary material
Rigorous ablations: Table 4 systematically validates necessity of factorized encoding, Neural ODEs, progressive training, and neighborhood regularization
weaknesses: Overstated physics claims: method learns latent state evolution, not physical laws; no constraints enforce conservation laws or physical principles; dynamic fields lack guaranteed interpretability as physical quantities

Limited generalization: cannot extrapolate beyond observed dynamics patterns; acknowledged limitation that method cannot predict motions deviating from training distribution significantly undermines 'physics-based' framing
Limited extrapolation distance: only 25% beyond observed frames (~1-2 seconds typical); no evaluation on longer horizons or out-of-distribution scenarios

Lack of physical validation: no quantitative physical plausibility metrics (energy/momentum conservation); Figure 3 visualization is qualitative; no comparison of predicted vs. ground truth accelerations/velocities

Incremental novelty: Neural ODEs, attention encoders, and dynamic 3DGS are established techniques; main contribution is their combination for particle-level dynamics, which is methodologically useful but conceptually incremental

Modest real-world performance: FreeGave-GoPro results show only ~0.3 dB improvement over velocity methods, suggesting method may exploit synthetic data characteristics or memorize training distribution

Insufficient justification for design choices: F=8 dynamic fields validated only empirically without theoretical analysis; progressive training schedule appears crucial but lacks principled motivation; neighborhood regularization seems like training workaround
Numerical stability not addressed: RK4 integration error accumulation over long extrapolation not discussed; single forward pass may struggle with stiff or rapidly changing dynamics
Missing analyses: why ParticleGS outperforms velocity fields unexplained; no failure case analysis; learned dynamics modes not visualized or interpreted; no ablation on extrapolation distance

strengths: Well-motivated conceptual framework contrasting time-conditioned deformation with physics-based state dynamics; toy experiment effectively demonstrates core insight
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across four datasets with detailed ablations and consistent improvements (~5 dB PSNR over time-conditioned methods on extrapolation)
Computationally efficient design: factorized state representation reduces complexity from O(NG) to O(FG), enabling scalability
Sound technical implementation: progressive training strategy, Neural ODE formulation appropriate for continuous dynamics, thorough architectural details provided
Clear presentation with effective visualizations and well-structured sections
weaknesses: Critical overclaiming: Repeatedly asserts method 'learns physical laws' and 'underlying physics' but only learns latent dynamics dg/dt=f(g,t) without enforcing conservation laws, physical constraints, or explicit physical principles. Latent dynamics ≠ physics; this is empirically-learned derivatives, not physics

Misleading framing: Claims 'prior-free' physics while factorization is motivated by Material Point Method (physics-informed). Also positions itself comparably to physics-enforcing methods like NVFi despite not embedding any governing equations

Insufficient mechanistic analysis: Doesn't isolate whether improvements derive from learning physics or simply from higher-order latent dynamics being more expressive than velocity fields. Ablation (3) removes continuous-time aspect entirely; fairer comparison would contrast against RNNs

Limited extrapolation evaluation: Only 25% observation window extrapolations tested; no error growth analysis over time; missing experiments on 1x/2x/3x extrapolation horizons to assess when performance diverges

Weak real-world validation: FreeGave-GoPro improvements marginal (0.28 dB PSNR on extrapolation); synthetic gains don't translate convincingly to actual video data, undermining claimed practical impact

Unfair velocity field comparison: ParticleGS uses 128D latent dynamics vs. first-order velocity fields; comparison confounds method expressiveness with physics understanding; no ablation isolating latent space expressiveness alone
Unjustified design choices: F=8 dynamic fields selected arbitrarily with no principled criterion; S=16, G=16 dimensions unexplained; no hyperparameter sensitivity analysis
Missing physics-enforcing baselines: OmniphysGS and Symplectic ODE-Net (referenced) embed actual physics but aren't compared; unclear how against methods actually incorporating physical constraints

Insufficient failure analysis: No examples of out-of-distribution failures; no sensitivity to observation length; limited discussion of when/why method fails; no analysis of error accumulation patterns
Statistical rigor: No confidence intervals, significance tests, or error bars; single runs reported; improvements may not be statistically significant

strengths: Clear problem motivation: identifies and articulates fundamental limitation of time-conditioned methods versus learning underlying dynamics
Sound technical approach: principled use of Neural ODEs for continuous dynamics with well-justified factorized state representation (O(NG) → O(FG))
Strong experimental results: 2-3 dB PSNR improvements on extrapolation across multiple datasets (Dynamic Objects, Indoor Scenes, Multipart, real-world FreeGave-GoPro)
Comprehensive evaluation: extensive comparisons against diverse baselines (time-conditioned, physics-prior, velocity-field), thorough ablations demonstrating component importance
Excellent presentation and reproducibility: clear architecture figures, complete implementation details, toy experiment provides good intuition, well-written
Practical engineering contributions: progressive training strategy, neighborhood regularization, sensible motion parametrization
Competitive rendering speed: maintains FPS comparable to velocity field methods while adding physics-based modeling
weaknesses: Limited novelty: individually components are well-established (Neural ODEs, factorized state from MPM, 3DGS). Primary contribution is a sensible engineering combination rather than novel concepts
Overclaimed 'prior-free' claim: method encodes several structural priors (factorization, motion decomposition, Rodrigues rotation formula). More accurate positioning needed

Insufficient validation of physical learning: no evidence that learned dynamics correspond to actual physics. Figure 3 visualization unclear; no comparison with physics simulators or ground-truth parameters

Weak theoretical justification for extrapolation: lacks argument for why learning dg_t/dt from observations enables extrapolation beyond training distribution. Assumption that dynamics remain constant during extrapolation is unvalidated

Limited extrapolation evaluation: all tests are short-term (25% extension). No systematic study of degradation with time horizon or failure mode analysis. Cannot assess when extrapolation becomes invalid
Incomplete analysis: arbitrary hyperparameters (F=8, k=32 neighbors); limited explanation of why Neural ODE >> MLP; no principled component selection strategy
Acknowledged limitations unaddressed: cannot predict out-of-distribution motions (e.g., breakage); no mechanism to detect failures. Significant practical limitation
Missing comparisons: OmniphysGS [33] cited but not compared; limited analysis of why velocity fields underperform. No long-horizon extrapolation results
Numerical stability not discussed: ODE integration stability over long horizons, stiff ODE handling, error accumulation not analyzed. Single-run results without confidence intervals
Physical interpretation unclear: what do the F learned dynamic fields represent? Are they approximating actual physical quantities or just fitting trajectories?
